before.overview: A 5-pitch, 800-ft moderate trad line up the right side of Cutthroat Wall, weaving through featured granite - corners, cracks and an easy alpine slab finish past a distinctive spiral tree - with multiple variations at nearly every pitch.

before.descent: Shared Cutthroat Wall descent: single-rope rappel from the notch to a ramp, then an ascending gully/ledge system on skier's left back to the base - study the beta carefully, as it's easy to get wrong.
before.descent_text: The descent has real potential to ruin your day if you don't study it beforehand. From the topout, reach the notch marked by a slung horn/tree between the westernmost and higher central buttress, rappel one rope-length over a chockstone tunnel to a dirty ramp with a small cave, then find the upward-trending gully/ledge system on skier's left (not the loose gully directly below) and follow it around back to the base.
before.rappels: Walk 100-200 ft along the summit ridge to a rap station; ~60m rappel angling rightward, then contour climbers' left around the head of a gully and circle back clockwise to the base. A single 60m rope often does not reach the ground on the final section.
